title: Suman Bhowmick
text:
PYTHON PROJECTS


A selection of Python-based data science and geospatial applications.


Each project combines clean code, visualizations, and analytical depth.





India Domestic Flights


Animated 24-hour map of 2,100 real domestic flights on Friday 01 March 2019 across 74 Indian airports using Bezier arc interpolation.


View More Details



India Night Lights


Monthly VIIRS-DNB satellite animation of India’s electrification from 2015 to 2025 using Google Earth Engine. Log-scaled, noise-masked and temporally smoothed.


View More Details



Migration Flows


Animated particle visualisation of inter-city migration across 36 Indian cities using Census 2011 data from Kaggle. Particles flow along Bezier arcs coloured by destination city.


View More Details



Urban Walkability


Measures daily-life accessibility on foot for Mumbai, London, Paris and Dubai using OSMnx isochrone analysis and OpenStreetMap POI data. Scores each city 0–100.


View More Details



Hospital Accessibility


Maps healthcare facility coverage across 12 major Indian cities using OSMnx and OpenStreetMap. Scores each city 0–100 based on hospital and clinic density within 5 km.


View More Details



India Demographics


Animated bubble chart tracing literacy, urbanisation and population across 35 Indian states from 1951 to 2011 using Census data from Kaggle.


View More Details



Road Networks


Visualisation of urban road networks for four major Indian cities using OSMnx and Matplotlib. Highlights spatial morphology through minimalist mapping

Step 6: Define city names and query boundaries

cities = ['Delhi', 'Mumbai', 'Chennai', 'Kolkata']
city_graphs = {}
city_boundaries = {}

for city in cities:
    # Get boundary polygon and street graph
    gdf = ox.geocode_to_gdf(city)
    city_boundaries[city] = gdf
    graph = ox.graph_from_place(city, network_type='drive')
    city_graphs[city] = graph



Step 7: Compute Road Network Metrics

projected_crs = "EPSG:32643"  # UTM zone for India (approx.)
metrics = []

for city in cities:
    G = city_graphs[city]
    boundary = city_boundaries[city]

    # Project the graph and boundary for accurate length/area calculation
    G_proj = ox.project_graph(G, to_crs=projected_crs)
    boundary_proj = boundary.to_crs(projected_crs)

    # Compute total area (in m²) of the boundary polygon
    total_area = boundary_proj.geometry.area.iloc[0]  # assuming one polygon

    # Compute basic graph statistics
    stats = ox.basic_stats(G_proj, clean_int_tol=15)

    # Build metrics row
    metrics.append({
        'City': city,
        'Total Street Length (km)': round(stats['edge_length_total'] / 1000, 2),
        'Street Density (km/km²)': round((stats['edge_length_total'] / 1000) / (total_area / 1e6), 2),
        'Intersection Density (/km²)': round(stats['intersection_count'] / (total_area / 1e6), 2),
        'Avg Streets per Node': round(stats.get('streets_per_node_avg', 0.0), 2),
    })



Step 8: Display metrics

metrics_df = pd.DataFrame(metrics)

print("\n📊 Network Metrics Summary:")
display(metrics_df)
